I was searching for a class combination that allows both 1 ≠ 0 and -1 ≠ 0 and expected something like docs#InvolutiveNeg + docs#NegZeroClass + NeZero 1 to work. But well, both InvolutiveNeg and NegZeroClass bundle a negation so having both gives you two different incompatible negations, which won't work. Furthermore, it seems like InvolutiveNeg + NegZeroClass would be the morally correct setting for docs#neg_eq_zero, which right now e.g. doesn't work for docs#EReal.
Should we just make both classes mixins? I don't feel like there are very good reasons to make these bundled and as mixins we could simply combine them for a more general neg_eq_zero.
I had exactly this problem while trying to make docs#neg_eq_zero work for docs#SignType
@loogle NegZeroClass _ → _
:search: NegZeroClass.toNeg, NegZeroClass.toZero, and 33 more
@loogle InvolutiveNeg _ → _
:search: InvolutiveNeg.toNeg, neg_neg, and 145 more
Well I guess the question is how we should handle deprecations if we go through with this change...

I mean there are still quite a few uses for each and all of them would have to add Zero and Neg hypotheses. If these were used very rarely we could probably just do the change without causing much trouble.
(and well I'm extrapolating here but many uses inside of mathlib probably also makes it's more likely to have many uses downstream)
So maybe we should go with just changing NegZeroClass first? Since that seems less used.
Or, I guess I haven't talked about the alternative of adding another class that extends both.
Not saying we shouldn't do this, but just noting that because of to_additive this is also a change to the multiplicative versions.
Yes of course; I guess a similar idea applies to docs#inv_eq_one.
Hmm one thought: What about having NegZeroClass extend InvolutiveNeg? Or do we care about a non-involutive negations that still have -0 = 0?
Matrices satisfy InvOneClass but not InvolutiveInv
Hmm good point
Wait but matrices are in a bit of weird position because they still have A⁻¹ = 1 ↔ A = 1, right?
I think so, but why is that a weird position? Basically their Inv is partial
Well, we still wouldn't be able to apply docs#inv_eq_one for matrices if we made it depend on InvOneClass and InvolutiveInv
That might not be too much of a big deal, though?

I think they also satisfy a⁻¹ = b ↔ a * b = 1 (docs#inv_eq_iff_mul_eq_one, docs#mul_eq_one_iff_inv_eq, docs#mul_eq_one_iff_inv_eq'), but those require Group
(the forward implication requires b ≠ 0 though)

Robin Arnez said:

Or, I guess I haven't talked about the alternative of adding another class that extends both.

Reminds me of #40855, so I vote for the mixins solution
So should InvolutiveNeg be a mixin or NegZeroClass or both?
I guess InvolutiveNeg has the advantage of having less operations involved (just one)
but NegZeroClass is used less often and a change would have less impact
MulOneClass is used a lot more than InvolutiveInv (based on a simple text search)
You mean InvOneClass?
Oh whoops, then I concur

I guess another argument for making NegZeroClass the mixin is that in SubNegZeroMonoid (the only class that extends NegZeroClass), the zero and negation are already provided by SubNegMonoid. On the other hand, HasDistribNeg extends InvolutiveNeg but doesn't already have a negation.
Alright, should I make a PR?

Snir Broshi said:

I think they also satisfy a⁻¹ = b ↔ a * b = 1 (docs#inv_eq_iff_mul_eq_one, docs#mul_eq_one_iff_inv_eq, docs#mul_eq_one_iff_inv_eq'), but those require Group
(the forward implication requires b ≠ 0 though)

This can't be true surely. Just take a noninvertible matrix a and define b to be a^{-1}, then LHS is true and RHS can't be.
but then you also don't have b ≠ 0
I opened #41907; it required a bit more adaptations than I hoped; but I've documented them all in the PR description.

ENNReal also satisfies both InvOneClass and InvolutiveInv so I'd expect a few more lemmas to be deleted / deprecated there. See also some previous discussions around these combinations of type classes in !3#16187 and #32614.
